input.summary:
Outbuildings part (carriage house + guest cottage) now writes only palette blocks: the carriage helper's "slate" roof is spelled deepslate_tile as each write is made, via a proxy in parts/outbuildings.mjs.
make.sh's outbuildings line is clean (1955 placed, no REFUSED, no OFF-PALETTE) and build.nbt is written.
The respell-after-the-fact pass is gone; the cottage code is unchanged.
left: The make.sh run still reports OFF-PALETTE for the mansion shell and roof (tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, polished_deepslate_slab and others, "fix roof.json"). They come from roof.json and the shell, not from parts/outbuildings.mjs, so I left them alone.

waste.what: Diagnosed the 288 slate_stairs report by hand: the palette check counts every write, including the hipRoof writes that the old respell pass overwrote afterwards, so the report looked like a real leak until I probed the part on a fresh grid.
waste.cost: 1 probe script, 2 Bash runs, about 4 tool calls
waste.tool: runParts' OFF-PALETTE report could list whether an off-palette write was later overwritten, or report the final grid's blocks instead of every write. Separately, hipRoof or carriageHouse could accept a palette roof material (slate -> deepslate_tile) so the helper never writes slate_stairs.

waste.what: Re-spelled the carriage house's roof stairs by scanning a 30x13x17 box cell by cell after the helper ran.
waste.cost: about 3,000 get calls on the old respell pass, now removed
waste.tool: A palette-aware write wrapper in the build library (the same spelling map that onPalette now carries locally), so every part can name roof materials by palette role instead of re-spelling.
